chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Husayni on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Uqbah who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan the Third (peace be upon him) asking him about the visitation of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and the visitation of Abu al-Hasan and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) wrote back to me: 'The former is preferred, and this is more complete and has greater reward.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Hasan, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Hadi, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْحُسَيْنُ: Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (Imam al-Husayn, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred shrine for visitation among the Imams according to Imam al-Hadi (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Ibrahim ibn Uqbah inquires about the comparative merit of visiting the shrines of the Imams, specifically highlighting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). Imam al-Hadi (a.s.) responds that while all visits are commendable, the visitation of Imam al-Husayn is 'more comprehensive' (muqaddam) and yields greater reward, reflecting the unique status of the 'Chief of the Youths of Paradise' in Shia devotional practice. This ruling underscores the theological emphasis on the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn as a central axis of Islamic history and spiritual merit.
